cases.name: Family preference and special-issuance sponsor note remain distinct
invariants: For several family applications, last-name spacing should be consistent unless a family member clearly prefers different spacing.
For special-issuance passports, an eligible family member's last-name spacing should match the sponsor's.
The explicit preference exception targets the general-family consistency recommendation.
Do not invent a must rule or resolve unstated precedence between the two notes.

cases.name: Generally insufficient rewrite grounds are not absolute or mandatory exceptions
invariants: Retain separate rules for spacing and suffix issues.
Generally not sufficient is weaker than an absolute prohibition.
Department disregard of a clear preference is an exception to the stated general rule.
The exception alone does not mandate or guarantee rewriting.
Retain 8 FAM 1001.2 as unresolved further guidance.

negative_controls.summary: A passport must never be rewritten for spacing or suffix issues.

cases.name: Might and generally survive without becoming universal duties
invariants: Retain the possible identity-evidence requirement under 22 CFR 51.23(c) and Department guidance.
Retain its purpose: establishing the name that best identifies the applicant.
Retain generally needing documentation to update the name on ID as practical qualified guidance.
Do not emit universal new-name-ID submission from might be required, and do not drop the weaker statements solely because they lack must.

cases.name: Source-supported tokens can still form a wrong semantic object
invariants: The applicant has had a material name change; DS-11 is the application form in the timing context.

cases.name: Definitions retain chapter, DS-2060, age and emancipation scope
invariants: Applicant includes the individual whose citizenship and identity are adjudicated, explicitly including DS-2060.
Minor applicants means un-emancipated applicants under 18, for purposes of this chapter.

cases.name: Suffix section boundaries and Sr. sense remain grounded
invariants: Convert Arabic ordinal name suffixes to Roman numerals; examples 2nd to II and 3rd to III are illustrative.

document.text:
8 FAM 403.1-4 Material Discrepancies (Major name changes)

(CT:CITZ-141; 03-10-2026)

a. A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5. The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

b. Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)). Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):

(1) Court orders or decrees:

(a) Name change orders; or

(b) Divorce decrees;

(2) Certificates of naturalization;

(3) Marriage certificates;

(4) Documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law; or

(5) Documentation of customary usage.

NOTE: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)

c. The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).

d. The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity. Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

(1) If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name. If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;

(2) The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID. You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL); and

(3) Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name. However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.

document.text:
NOTE: The term “applicant” is used hereinafter for the individual whose citizenship and identity is being adjudicated, including for form DS-2060. For purposes of this chapter, minor applicants are defined as un-emancipated applicants under the age of 18.

8 FAM 403.1-4 Material Discrepancies (Major name changes)

(CT:CITZ-141; 03-10-2026)

a. A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5. The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

b. Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)). Acceptable means of documenting a material name change include (per 22 CFR 51.25):

(1) Court orders or decrees:

(a) Name change orders; or

(b) Divorce decrees;

(2) Certificates of naturalization;

(3) Marriage certificates;

(4) Documentation demonstrating change of name by operation of state law; or

(5) Documentation of customary usage.

NOTE: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)

c. The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).

d. The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity. Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

(1) If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name. If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;

(2) The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID. You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL); and

(3) Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name. However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.

c. The court order or decree must be final:

(1) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in her/his new name. See 8 FAM 1001.5 regarding applying for a replacement passport in a new name;

(2) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a form FS-240 in her/his new name. See 8 FAM 1001.3 regarding amending a form FS-240; and

(3) You must clear the applicant's pending name even though the name change is not final and even if the passport is not being issued at this time.

d. The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).

EXCEPTION: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program). When this occurs, the applicant must provide both her/his current and former names on the application. You may request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity in accordance with 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.

8 FAM 403.1-3(B) Name Spacing

(CT:CITZ-96; 08-04-2023)

a. In accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) recommendations, U.S. passports, form FS-240, and form DS-2060 are printed in all uppercase letters. Printing a name with multiple parts in uppercase letters causes the name to appear as one word unless the parts are separated with spaces. Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:

(1) If the applicant's previous passport had a space, you should add a space on the current application;

(2) If the applicant does not have a previous passport and the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or ID has a space, you should add a space on the current application; or

(3) If the applicant expresses a clear preference to add or remove space, either verbally or in writing, you may add or remove it per the applicant's preference.

NOTE: If you receive applications from several family members, you should space the last names consistently, unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.

NOTE: For special-issuance passports, the spacing of an eligible family member's last name should match the spacing of the last name of the sponsor.

b. Name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).

c. Arabic ordinal numbers must be changed to Roman numerals, for example, 2nd to II, 3rd to III:

d. Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English. If you determine that this is the case, follow the guidance in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles.

e. Name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
